system_note: What was billed: Principal = M72.6 (Necrotizing fasciitis, POA=Y, MCC). Claim also bills R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock, MCC), J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, MCC), J80 (ARDS, MCC, POA=N), Z99.11 (dependence on respirator status, POA=N), and G93.6 (cerebral edema, POA=N), plus organism codes (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) and multiple diabetes/complication codes. What the record shows (selected citations): - Necrotizing fasciitis is well supported on admission by imaging and operative management: the H&P documents that "CT scan confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 541) The CT impression documents "Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes." (IV Contrast, Chart Notes, p. 421) General surgery likewise documents a Type II necrotizing soft-tissue infection requiring immediate operative debridement. (General Surgery Consultation - Emergent, Chart Notes, p. 46). These citations meet the policy validation criteria that require operative or imaging confirmation of fascial plane necrosis to code M72.6 (Policy: Necrotizing Fasciitis - operative confirmation: "Gross fascial necrosis observed intraoperatively: gray, non-viable fascia ..."). (Policy Documents/DRG/Necrotizing Fasciitis.docx, Validation Criteria - Surgical Pathway) - Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21) is supported by provider documentation of septic shock, high lactate on arrival, and vasopressor therapy in the ICU (H&P shows lactate 8.6 mmol/L and describes septic shock; Critical Care note documents vasopressors on and P/F 63 with lactate 4.9). (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 541; Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, p. 84). Sepsis policy requires provider documentation and vasopressor/lactate evidence to support R65.21; the record documents both (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx: vasopressor requirement such as norepinephrine satisfies Criterion 2). (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Medical - Septic Shock Confirmed on Admission Pathway) - Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (J96.01) is supported by documented invasive mechanical ventilation and objective hypoxemia (ABG/P/F) in the critical care notes (Critical Care Progress Note: "ABG (02:00): pH 7.28 / PaCO2 45 / PaO2 60 / HCO3 19; Lac: 4.9 | P/F 63.") The ARF policy includes a presumption rule that initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure satisfies objective hypoxemia documentation when pre-intubation room-air measurements are not available. (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx, Validation Criteria - Medical Pathway) - ARDS (J80) is supported as a hospital-developed complication: admission portable CXR shows no pulmonary abnormality, and later imaging and consults document bilateral opacities and ARDS management (Nephrology consult: "Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Bilateral opacities compatible with ARDS."; Discharge summary documents ARDS with prone positioning). This timeline supports POA=N for J80, consistent with the ARDS policy requirements for bilateral opacities plus a clinical risk factor (sepsis) and P/F thresholds/ventilator settings. (Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 779; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 845; Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS).docx) Finding(s) requiring correction and why (with record citations): 1) G93.6 - Cerebral edema (billed, POA=N, MCC): unsupported. There is no provider documentation or imaging report in the retrieved chart text that documents "cerebral edema" or operative/consult confirmation. Discharge/transfer diagnoses and the hospital problem list-comprehensive summaries of the ICU course-list septic shock, ARDS, AKI, DKA and many complications but do not list cerebral edema; the discharge summary documents resolution of septic shock and ARDS without mentioning cerebral edema. (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 845; Hospital Problem List, p. 330). Because policy for a diagnosis like cerebral edema requires explicit provider documentation or imaging confirmation, absence of any such documentation means G93.6 lacks clinical support and should be removed. (No policy rule for G93.6 was provided in the retrieved policies; absence of supporting clinician documentation is dispositive under auditing standards.) 2) Z99.11 - Dependence on respirator [ventilator] status (billed POA=N): appears to be inappropriately active at discharge. The discharge/transfer documentation shows the patient transferred to LTAC on nasal cannula / tolerating trach collar and ambulatory: "Condition & Functional Status at Transfer Alert, oriented, and interactive. Nasal cannula 2 L." and the Transfer Instructions explicitly list transfer to a Long-Term Acute Care Hospital. (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 845; Transfer Instructions, Discharge / Transfer Instructions, p. 843). Dependence-on-ventilator codes are status codes that should reflect ongoing ventilator dependence; the record at transfer documents only trach collar tolerance and low-flow oxygen, not continued ventilator dependence for home use. Unless there is a separate note explicitly documenting ongoing ventilator dependence at discharge/transfer (which was not retrieved), Z99.11 should be removed. If the facility intended to report home-ventilator dependence, provider documentation specifically stating dependence for discharge/transfer is required. (See hospital Problem List entries noting "vent-dependent" earlier are inconsistent with the discharge status and should be reconciled by CDI/coder.) What should remain coded (supported): M72.6; R65.21; J96.01; J80 (POA=N); organism codes (culture/ID note supports Streptococcus pyogenes and MRSA: "Deep tissue cultures growing Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus." (Infectious Diseases Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 341)); diabetes and related comorbidity codes. Procedural coding (endotracheal intubation, debridements, split-thickness skin graft, PICC insertion, arterial monitoring, ventilation >96 hours, platelet transfusion) is supported by operative/surgery and ICU notes and the discharge summary (e.g., emergent debridement x3, STSG on ICU day 18, mechanical ventilation and prolonged ICU course). (General Surgery Consultation - Emergent, Chart Notes, p. 46; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 845; History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 541). Corrective action taken in this audit: Remove unsupported diagnoses G93.6 and Z99.11 from the claim's diagnosis list and leave all other billed diagnoses and procedures in place pending provider attestation or further CDI clarification. (If the provider can produce explicit documentation that cerebral edema or continued ventilator dependence were present at transfer/discharge, those codes may be reinstated.) Evidence citations (selected) used to reach this determination are provided below in the Evidence section for direct auditability.
rationale_letter: Re: DRG review - Claim MR_13 Dear Provider/Coding Team, We completed a clinical documentation and coding audit for inpatient claim MR_13 (admission 05/18/2026). The audit compared the claim's billed diagnoses and procedures against the medical record and the payer's DRG validation policy. Based on the chart review and policy guidance, we are issuing a Finding requiring correction to the claim's coded diagnosis list. Finding: Two billed diagnoses lack adequate clinical support and should be removed from the claim: 1. G93.6 - Cerebral edema (billed POA=N): The medical record contains no provider note, imaging report, or consultant documentation that explicitly documents "cerebral edema." The discharge/transfer summary and hospital problem list-comprehensive summaries of the course-do not list cerebral edema among the admission or discharge diagnoses. Because coding for cerebral edema requires explicit clinician documentation or confirmatory imaging, G93.6 is not supported by the retrieved medical record and should be removed. 2. Z99.11 - Dependence on respirator [ventilator] status (billed POA=N): At transfer/discharge the patient is documented as tolerating a tracheostomy collar and receiving low-flow supplemental oxygen (nasal cannula 2 L) and was transferred to a Long-Term Acute Care Hospital for wound care and rehabilitation. The record excerpts reviewed do not document ongoing ventilator dependence at discharge (the status code Z99.11 should reflect persistent ventilator dependence). Therefore, Z99.11 should be removed unless explicit provider documentation is produced showing ventilator dependence at discharge/transfer. Basis / Evidence (selected): - Imaging and operative/source-control documentation confirming necrotizing fasciitis: "CT scan confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 541) and "Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes." (IV Contrast, Chart Notes, p. 421). The treating surgeons documented an urgent debridement for Type II necrotizing NSTI. (General Surgery Consultation - Emergent, Chart Notes, p. 46). Policy requires operative or imaging confirmation of fascial necrosis to validate M72.6 (Policy Documents/DRG/Necrotizing Fasciitis.docx). - Septic shock, organism identification and respiratory failure are supported: deep tissue cultures grew Group A Streptococcus and MRSA ("Deep tissue cultures growing Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus." - Infectious Diseases Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 341), septic shock with elevated lactate and vasopressors is documented (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 541; Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, p. 84) satisfying R65.21 policy criteria. ARDS developed after admission with bilateral opacities documented later (Nephrology Consultation: "Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Bilateral opacities compatible with ARDS." - Chart Notes, p. 779) supporting J80 as POA=N. Mechanical ventilation and ABG/P/F data support J96.01 under the ARF policy presumption for intubated patients. Correction required: Remove G93.6 and Z99.11 from the claim's diagnosis list. Leave the remaining diagnoses and procedures as billed (including M72.6 as principal diagnosis), because those entries are supported by imaging, operative notes, cultures, ICU notes, and the facility's discharge summary. The corrected complete diagnosis list (position 1 = principal) we are recording for this audit is: [M72.6, A49.59, R65.21, E11.10, E87.2, J96.01, J80, N17.9, A49.02, B95.62, L03.115, E11.65, E11.22, E11.40, I10, E78.5, F32.9]. The corrected procedure list remains the same as billed. If you believe additional documentation exists in the medical record (for example, an operative report or imaging report documenting cerebral edema, or a discharge note explicitly documenting ongoing ventilator dependence at transfer) please provide that documentation so we may reassess. Otherwise, the two diagnoses noted above should be removed from the final claim submission. Sincerely, Clinical Documentation and Coding Audit Team
